title: Language comparison checked against known LP readings
question: Does the eight-language length comparison recognize the established English readings of Liber Primus?
summary: Nine known reading sections and their pool. English is closest for the pool, but some short sections rank other profiles first; the LP2-56 hash demonstrates an input-selection problem.

scope.representation: All nine known reading sections; headings included; slash/CR/LF wraps removed within sections. Unfiltered literal labels retained as diagnostic; amended rune-derived labels and native rune lengths; sections pooled without boundary joining.
scope.procedure: Replay fixed known readings exactly. Compare all section/pool length histograms with all eight FLORES dev language profiles under letter, folded and GP grouping models. Check independently using archived traces, regex tokenization and rational distances.
scope.parameters: Nine sections, 17 pages; 10 targets including the pool; 70 profiles, 90 eight-language rankings; bins 1–15 and 16+; all 997 development sentences per language. Original plan plus post-diagnostic amendment.
scope.exclusions: No blind decryption, posterior, accuracy inference from independent random trials, new language labels for solved sections, or authentication of source readings. No new unknown-page results. GP grouping is an orthographic sensitivity.

finding: The pooled 739 native rune tokens rank closest to English in every comparison, but some individual known-English sections do not. Removing 38 non-rune alphabetic characters from LP2-56 changes its literal-profile comparison; the hash had doubled its apparent word count from 25 to 50.
limitations: Sections contain 18–208 native tokens and are not independent random samples. The pool reuses the sections. Literal spelling, symbol units and embedded material affect rankings. The amendment followed inspection of the first run; human review pending.
next_steps: Review conversion/boundary choices; add a fixed genre-matched parallel corpus and exact target-size calibration. Do not infer plaintext language from a short-section nearest match.
